public_rationale: There is relevant evidence behind the concern: research found narrowing thematic diversity and unequal access to the resources needed for deep learning. But these findings do not establish the asserted displacement of numerous alternative ideas. The thematic study explicitly identifies causal attribution as unfinished work. The evidence neither settles nor refutes the causal claim.
limitations: The wording is metaphorical and framed as a concern.
Institutional exclusion and displacement of research ideas are different outcomes.
The claim does not commit to the superiority of the alternatives.

statement.document_title: AGI will not happen in your lifetime. Or will it?

from_speaker: I’ve been concerned for a long time
a fixation on Big Data has sucked the oxygen
from a lot of other ideas
our_interpretation: I assess the embedded causal assertion, not whether Marcus sincerely held this concern.
The ordinary reading is that prioritizing data-intensive AI materially displaced funding, staffing, or research attention from numerous alternative approaches.
'Might be better' does not assert that those alternatives were demonstrably superior.
The claim concerns a developing pattern before publication, with no stated beginning. I retain an unspecified start rather than inventing a fixed historical interval.
criteria.support_condition: Research or institutional records establish that prioritizing data-intensive approaches caused material displacement of support for numerous alternative AI approaches.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, credible causal evidence shows that the alleged prioritization did not materially displace alternative approaches, or that the apparent displacement was attributable to other causes.
